learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the basic principles of vehicle dynamics, and their application to calculations and analyses related to the dynamic behavior of automobiles.
Study of the design and operation of the main systems and components of automotive vehicles.
Analysis of the regulations affecting vehicles, and the procedures for the legalization of automobiles and their modifications.
Study of the norms and guidelines to follow in carrying out the most common vehicle modification projects.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of Mechanical Engineering aimed at the construction, modification, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge of the principles of machine and mechanism theory.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.

syllabus_topics: Regulations, legalization, and technical inspection of automobiles.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical multiple-choice questions (Part A of exam)
Numerical problem solving and practical cases (Part B of exam)
Tutored resolution of practical vehicle dynamics cases
Analysis of practical cases on vehicle modifications and application of regulations
Attendance to visits and other voluntary activities

assessment_rules: The exam consists of two parts: theoretical multiple-choice questions (A) and numerical problem-solving and practical cases (B). The exam grade is the arithmetic mean of parts A and B (50% each), requiring a minimum score of 4 in each part to be averaged. For students following continuous evaluation, the final grade is a weighted average of the exam grade (75%) and the continuous evaluation grade (25%). If continuous evaluation is not applicable, the exam grade constitutes 100% of the final grade.
